title: Expense receipt capture
status: dev: generator 1.1.0 (review fixes 2026-10-21: correction re-checks, approval and repost traps, oracle email layout and Amount format, reference departures), oracle, observable-only reference, controls and gates built; no arm has run (no model, $0)

grounding.gives: free-text receipt messages in #expense-submissions ('Expense: <what>, $<amount>, category: <C>, date: <YYYY-MM-DD>'); an Expense Tracker spreadsheet with a Submissions worksheet and an Expense Policy worksheet (Allowed Categories: Travel, Meals, Office Supplies, Software, Consulting; Rejected Categories: Entertainment, Personal, Gifts, which need VP pre-approval outside the channel; a $75 per person meal limit above which the attendee count is needed); log accepted receipts, a thread reply confirming what was logged or why it was rejected; the escape-room trap (Entertainment, $890) and 'Uber to airport' (Travel)

the expense limits: hotel $250 per night domestic and $350 international (per-night arithmetic over several nights), meals $75 per person for team meals and $50 individual, economy flights unless the trip exceeds 6 hours (a business class 5-hour flight is a violation), no alcohol except client entertainment with the client's name ('Drinks at conference' is alcohol), manager pre-approval over $500, receipts required over $25 (an $18 cable without a receipt is fine)

stateOfRecord: The #expense-submissions channel (receipts, their threads, corrections, pre-approvals and the automation's replies), the Submissions worksheet (one row per logged receipt: Message TS, Submitted, Employee, Date, Amount, Category, Attendees, Status) and the Employees worksheet (Email, Manager Email); all in the world, visible to every arm. Daily meal totals, pending pre-approvals and reposts are read back from them
envelope: google_sheets.values.append one Submissions row per receipt that passes (Status Approved or Pending Pre-Approval), or per rejected receipt that a correction makes pass
google_sheets.values.update the receipt's own Submissions row (a correction by its poster; a pre-approval by the poster's manager)
slack.message.post in #expense-submissions, in the receipt's thread: 'Logged: $<amount> <Category>', 'Pending pre-approval: $<amount> <Category>' or 'Rejected: <reason>'
gmail.message.send to finance@company.example.com at week close ('Weekly expense totals <week_start>')
slack.message.post in #automation-review (escalation only: a poster missing from Employees)
harmless: a thread parent's reply_count (Slack sets it when a reply is posted)
read flags or labels on mail already in the mailbox

receipt.corrected.note: d2: a correction that fixes a rejected receipt (attendee count or receipt), and one more: a change to a logged receipt that keeps it logged (amount, date, a category declared wrongly) or one whose re-check decides (amount over $500: pending; attendee count lowered: rejected; a hotel declared Consulting corrected to Travel; a pending receipt's amount changed; a pre-approved receipt's amount changed; a second correction in the thread); half the seeds one from someone other than the poster. d3 always: the rejected-receipt fix, one more as at d2, a wrong-person correction, an individual meal raised over $50 (rejected; a later meal that day must not count it), the last meal of a capped day changed (the cap's own-row rule), a second correction with a relative date, a pre-approved receipt corrected (still approved), and an approved receipt raised over $500 after the manager's premature 'pre-approved' (pending)

receipt.reposted.note: the same employee, expense date and amount in other words (amount and date styles change); d2: one repost of last week's receipt and (3 reposts) a terse one without description or category; d3: a repost of a receipt rejected for its missing receipt, now with the file; a repost with an explicit date of a receipt dated 'today' or 'yesterday' on an earlier day; a repost 'yesterday' of a receipt dated explicitly the day before; and (4 reposts) a plain, last-week or terse one

preapproval.reply.note: the manager's pre-approval (sometimes of last week's pending receipt); d2: half the seeds its repeat, half the seeds one more from the wrong person, a negated one, or the manager's on a receipt that is not pending; d3: the manager's, its repeat, a namesake of the manager, 'Not pre-approved yet', and the manager's 'pre-approved' on a receipt logged Approved at once (later corrected over $500)

week.close.at: Friday 16:00 UTC; the last trigger, it carries the end-of-week grading

trapRates.unit: measured share of receipt.posted triggers carrying a trap label (context labels such as plain rule rejections excluded); corrections, reposts, pre-approvals and the week close carry state traps by construction

measuredTriggerShare.on: seeds 601-650, mean of per-stream shares, generator 1.1.0

T-format: synonym (category written as a word of the table, 'Rideshare', 'Lodging', 'Team building', or not written at all: the table decides)
declared-category (a category written explicitly that the description contradicts: the written one decides until the poster corrects it)
date-format (Mar 4, March 4, 4 March, today, yesterday, no date)
drinks (alcohol words: rejected without a client name, accepted with one)
flight-long (business over 6 hours: allowed, then pending over $500)
approval-negated ('Not pre-approved yet' from the manager: nothing)
correction-relative-date ('Correction: the date was yesterday' posted on a later day than the receipt: read on the correction's day)
cabin-lookalike ('for a business meeting', '(business trip)' on a flight with no cabin: economy)
T-authority: wrong-corrector (a 'Correction' from someone other than the poster: nothing)
wrong-approver ('pre-approved' from the employee, another manager, a namesake, Finance: nothing)
unknown-poster (a contractor not in Employees: escalate)
T-lookalike: namesake (the approver shares the manager's first name)
display-name (the poster's Slack name is a nickname; the row takes the Employees name)
manager-display-name (the manager's Slack name is shortened; the approval still counts)
T-repeat: repost (the same receipt in other words: nothing)
repost-history (a repost of last week's receipt)
repost-fixed (a rejected receipt reposted with its file: still a repost)
near-dup (same description and amount on another date, another amount the same day, or another employee: processed normally)
approval-again (a second pre-approval after the first: nothing)
approval-not-pending (the manager's 'pre-approved' on a receipt logged Approved at once: nothing)
repost-rel, repost-rel-rev, repost-relative (each message read relative to its own posting date: an earlier 'today' reposted later with an explicit date, and the reverse)
near-dup-relative (the same words 'today' or 'yesterday' on a later day: another expense date, processed)
repost-terse (a repost without description or category: nothing, before any category reading)
T-state: meal-cap (individual meals of the day over $100: rejected)
cap-history (the cap counts last week's rows for the same expense date)
cap-under (meals of the day near the cap but within it)
correction-fix (a correction makes a rejected receipt pass: append its row)
approval-history (last week's pending receipt approved this week)
approved-last-week (approved this week, not in this week's totals)
corrected-total (a corrected row counts with its new amount)
correction-recheck (the re-check makes the corrected receipt Pending or Rejected, not Logged)
correction-own-row (a corrected individual meal: the cap counts the other rows, not its own old row)
correction-multi (a second correction in a thread: the first still applies)
correction-preapproved (a pre-approval given earlier in the thread still counts after a correction)
correction-early-approval (a 'pre-approved' given while the row was Approved does not count when a correction makes it pending)
correction-travel-facts (a hotel declared Consulting and corrected to Travel: the hotel rule applies)
cap-rejected-row (a later individual meal of the day: the cap skips the row a correction rejected)
total-rejected-row (the weekly totals skip a row a correction rejected)

judgment.what: reading a free-text receipt (POLICY.md section 7): amount (digits, USD or words), expense date (ISO, month names, today, yesterday), category (written or from the word table), attendee count, receipt, alcohol, client name, hotel nights and international, flight cabin and duration
judgment.narrow: one typed extraction per message (and per correction); the reference reads it with a small parser, a workflow arm would use one typed Haiku call and code for every rule
judgment.share: every receipt; about one in five carries a format trap at d3

hypothesis.label: either: workflow at high N
hypothesis.workflow: a workflow with one typed Haiku extraction per message and the rules in code about 0.9 or better
hypothesis.why: Each receipt is easy for an agent: one message, two lookups (the poster's Employees row, the Submissions rows), eight table rules and one exact reply. The cross-trigger state is where a per-trigger agent must rebuild context every time and where a workflow pays: the daily meal cap across messages and weeks, pending pre-approvals and who may approve them, corrections that re-check and update in place, and reposts compared against the channel's history.

heldout.note: never generated or inspected by the family author; gen.py and harness.py refuse seeds outside 601-650

seeds.difficultyRule: within each seed block the first seed is d2, then d2/d3 alternate (gen.default_difficulty); --difficulty overrides
